sourceOccurrences.label: Boundary crossing profile
sourceOccurrences.note: PTM2 counts the nested cube boundaries crossed by one displacement and proves the averaged boundary-functional inequality for the actual bond-probability profile.

sourceOccurrences.label: Cube boundary geometry
sourceOccurrences.note: 31X5 proves an exact displacement count for boundary pairs and the power-law shell comparisons. The logarithm is log(en) at every positive integer scale; the source endpoint correction is provisional.

sourceOccurrences.label: Critical box lower bound
sourceOccurrences.note: VVB0 combines the profile inequality with the existing critical flux theorem R84Z. It retains internal versus unrestricted connections and finite critical intensity.

sourceOccurrences.label: Critical exponent lower bounds
sourceOccurrences.note: BNQK uses the existing UVQ6 window bound and makes the epsilon passage from logarithmic exponents explicit. Existence of the tail and pointwise exponents are separate hypotheses.

sourceOccurrences.label: Matching spatial averages
sourceOccurrences.note: 0BJP combines VVB0 with MRZO for globally comparable kernels. It also records the logarithmic growth exponent at alpha=1 without removing the logarithmic gap.

sourceOccurrences.label: Probability inputs and finite-window estimates
sourceOccurrences.note: 12NL proves the rooted damping used in UVQ6; UVQ6 gives the required quantile and first-moment scales from the uniform full-cluster tail. R84Z supplies critical flux. The source steps are not duplicated as new tags.

proofUses.reason: Count integer radii with one endpoint inside and the other outside; use monotonicity of internal connections and Tonelli.
Shell counting estimates the crossing profile; exact product intersection counts compare it with the expected open boundary.
Critical flux is at least one for every box; average and divide by the positive crossing profile.
Uniform global tails imply window-tail bounds. Compare finite-window hyperscaling with the critical box lower bound, then pass from slightly weaker polynomial estimates to logarithmic exponents.
A lower kernel envelope supplies the finite critical point and sharp averaged upper bound; the upper envelope supplies the lower bound.
